Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". With the power to approve codes and the enforcement of approved codes repealed on June 14, 1935, the clause had nothing left to operate on; the resolution states no later effective date, and no held record ends the clause earlier.

Rule 1 permits certificated incapacitated persons to do homework at factory wage rates; it is an exception to code prohibitions of homework and applies only where a code prohibits homework, as the closing paragraph states, so it operated only through approved codes. research_rationale:
Executive Order 6711-A of May 15, 1934 prescribes rules for how the labor provisions of approved codes of fair competition apply to certain homeworkers and operates as a condition on previous code-approval orders. Every command in it operates on, or through, codes approved under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA): the rules govern how code provisions are construed and applied, rule 2 requires filing with the Code Authority, and the closing paragraph makes the order binding on those subject to codes that prohibit homework and a condition on approval orders. The order's own duration clause says it remains in effect 'until revoked or modified by my further order or by order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery'; that is a continuing term with no date, and no held record shows a revocation or modification before June 14, 1935. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, which removed the approved codes these rules operate on; the best supported first end is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No held record shows these rules revoked, modified, suspended or superseded before June 14, 1935. I read the full order; its only own-terms duration language is 'shall remain in effect until revoked or modified by my further order or by order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery', which states no date. The lookups report no held order text citing this order by number, and a search of the held order texts for 'homework' finds only this order and Executive Order 6756-B (a Puerto Rico needlework code whose wage provisions mention homeworkers); neither revokes or modifies it. Executive Order 6750-C (apprentice rules) is a separate order that does not name this one. An order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery would not appear among held presidential orders, so the held corpus cannot exclude one; no held source indicates that one exists. The WPA list entry (1934 May 15, p.578) records the rules as prescribed. The OFR catalog starts in 1937, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.","independent_command_check":"No clause is independent of the codes. Rule 1 creates an exception to code prohibitions of homework; rule 2 directs employers to file with the Code Authority, a body of an approved code; the closing paragraph binds only those 'subject to Codes of Fair Competition in which homework is prohibited' and conditions code-approval orders. There is no appointment, delegation, report requirement or committee. The order cites 'Title I' generally rather than a numbered section; I treat it as code-dependent because of those terms, and a reviewer should test that characterization, which the shared analysis does not decide for general rule-prescribing orders.","savings_check":"Savings are accrued effects only: certificates and acts before the repeal. savings.reason: Homework certificates issued, and acts done in reliance on the rules, before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for pre-repeal action under codes is accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso whose effect the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the rules after June 14, 1935.
